Claude might not have improved my results directly.
Results still come down to execution, position size & sitting through the trade. What changed is speed. That matters more for me than most, because I do all this around a full-time job. 
Work that ate a weekend now fits into an evening.

Where I actually use it:

1. Chart Playbook database
Every setup I save gets logged with its context - pattern, ADR%, prior move, where it sat against the 11/21 EMA, what happened next. Claude keeps it structured & searchable, so I can pull up every NR7 near a 52-week high I've ever marked instead of scrolling through a folder of screenshots.

2. Obsidian + Claude Code
My second brain. Transcripts, strategy notes, setups & catalyst logs all go in, searchable & cross-linked. Everything below pulls from this.

3. Backtesting
Pine Script systems across NSE & NASDAQ. Parameter studies, pre-breakout fingerprints, plus the exit-rule test I still owe myself. This is probably best usage considering as I have no background of Coding 

4. Research
Concall analysis in a fixed format. Single-company deep dives. One running thread per name, revisited each quarter. Balance sheet template. Sometimes ranking a shortlist.

5. Dashboards
Core/Satellite portfolio. Market breadth - Stockbee-style, tuned to NSE. Python + Kite Connect + GitHub Actions.

6. TradingView
MCP link for quant studies off the charts, plus Pine Screener.

7. Journal review
TradesViz exports read against my edge. Hold time, R-multiples, which setup paid, whether I followed the plan. This produced my current 4-rule protocol.

8. Earnings calendar
Watchlist dates tracked, so nothing I hold surprises me.

9. Cowork
Monthly journal review or a 4-quarter concall batch, start to finish, while I'm at work.

10. YouTube content
Scripts, articles, posts, thumbnails, chart animations.

Edge is mine. Claude just removes everything standing between me & running it.
Please share any other use cases you guys run which I can utilize.

A simple exercise:

Open a chart and look at the last 20 daily candles.

Ask…

- are buyers becoming more aggressive?
- are sellers becoming weaker?
- is volume expanding on green days?
- is volume drying up on red days?
- how tight is price action?

Don't overcomplicate it.

You're simply trying to determine whether pressure is building or releasing.

Want to Know If the Market Is Topping or Just Resetting for the Next Leg Higher? Read this.

Stan Weinstein’s framework gives us one of the simplest ways to answer it.

The Nasdaq ran 34% from the March low to the June high.

Then it spent three months going nowhere.The key is the 30-week moving average.

Stage 2 pause:
- 30-week MA still rising
- Price holds above it, pullbacks find support near the line
- Down weeks come on lighter volume
- The range eventually resolves higher

Stage 3 top:
- 30-week MA flattens out
- Price whips above and below the line
- Heavy volume shows up on down weeks
- Rallies keep failing at the same level

Right now, $QQQ sits above a 30-week line that is still rising.

By Weinstein’s framework, that looks more like a Stage 2 pause than a Stage 3 top.

That can change. The line flattening is the tell.

Until it does, the trend gets the benefit of the doubt.

Sideways above a rising line = pause.
Sideways through a flat line = potential top.

The market doesn’t need to go up every week to remain in an uptrend.

Sometimes the strongest moves come after months of doing nothing. We’ve seen this again and again - October 2023, April 2025, November 2025, and March 2026 are some of the best examples.

Until the 30-week MA tells us otherwise, the primary trend remains intact.
